Find the $y$-intercepts of the circle $(x-2)^{2}+(y-4)^{2}=9,$ shown above.

feedback.worked_solution:
We must have $x=0$ at the $y$-intercepts. 

So, we need to substitute $x=0$ into the equation of the circle and solve the resulting equation for $y,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}-x+4y & =5 \\ {0}^{2}+{y}^{2}-0+4y & =5 \\ {y}^{2}+4y & =5\end{aligned}
$$

We can solve this equation by completing the square, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{2}+4y+4 & =5+4 \\ (y+2)^{2} & =9 \\ y+2 & =\pm 3 \\ y & =-2\pm 3.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $y$-intercepts occur at the points $(0,-5)$ and $(0,1),$ as shown below.
